No one has ever filled the place left vacant by John Maddison Morton. arxiv-2011-11630.title: Betrayed by Motion: Camouflaged Object Discovery via Motion Segmentation
arxiv-2011-11630.creator: Hala Lamdouar, Charig Yang, Weidi Xie, Andrew Zisserman
arxiv-2011-11630.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Hala Lamdouar, Charig Yang, Weidi Xie, Andrew Zisserman. The objective of this paper is to design a computational architecture that discovers camouflaged objects in videos, specifically by exploiting motion information to perform object segmentation.

arxiv-2101-00357.title: How do mobility restrictions and social distancing during COVID-19 affect the crude oil price?
arxiv-2101-00357.creator: Asim K. Dey, Kumer P. Das
arxiv-2101-00357.description: Abstract We develop an air mobility index and use the newly developed Apple’s driving trend index to evaluate the impact of COVID-19 on the crude oil price. We use quantile regression and stationary and non-stationary extreme value models to study the impact.

arxiv-2208-06414.title: Optimistic No-regret Algorithms for Discrete Caching CCS: Networks Network performance analysis
arxiv-2208-06414.creator: Naram Mhaisen, Abhishek Sinha, Georgios Paschos, George Iosifidis
arxiv-2208-06414.description: Abstract . We take a systematic look at the problem of storing whole files in a cache with limited capacity in the context of optimistic learning, where the caching policy has access to a prediction oracle (provided by, e.g., a Neural Network).

arxiv-2208-10871.title: Probing system size dependence at high baryon density by systematic comparison of Ag+Ag and Au+Au reactions at 1.23 A A GeV
arxiv-2208-10871.creator: Tom Reichert 1,3 , Apiwit Kittiratpattana 1,4 , Pengcheng Li 1,5,6 , Jan Steinheimer 7 , Marcus Bleicher 1,2,3
arxiv-2208-10871.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tom Reichert 1,3 , Apiwit Kittiratpattana 1,4 , Pengcheng Li 1,5,6 , Jan Steinheimer 7 , Marcus Bleicher 1,2,3. We present UrQMD predictions for the comparison of the recently measured Ag+Ag and Au+Au runs at a beam energy of E lab E_{\mathrm{lab}} = 1.23 A A GeV explored by the HADES experiment.

arxiv-2212-11925.title: The SUSY Index Beyond the Cardy Limit
arxiv-2212-11925.creator: Ohad Mamroud
arxiv-2212-11925.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ohad Mamroud. We analyze a set of contributions to the superconformal index of 4d 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) super Yang-Mills using the Bethe Ansatz approach. These contributions dominate at the large N N limit, where their leading order in N N reproduces various supersymmetric Euclidean black hole saddles in the dual theory, and they also dominate for finite N N in high temperature Cardy-like limits.

arxiv-2305-19050.creator: János Barát
arxiv-2305-19050.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by János Barát. In an orientation O O of the graph G G , an arc e e is deletable if and only if O − e O-e is strongly connected. For a 3 3 -edge-connected graph G G , the Frank number is the minimum k k for which G G admits k k strongly connected orientations such that for every edge e e of G G the corresponding arc is deletable in at least one of the k k orientations.

arxiv-2309-07549.title: A single layer representation of the scattered field for multiple scattering problems
arxiv-2309-07549.creator: Didier Felbacq, Anthony Gourdin and Emmanuel Rousseau
arxiv-2309-07549.description: Abstract The scattering of scalar waves by a set of scatterers is considered. It is proven that the scattered field can be represented as an integral supported by any smooth surface enclosing the scatterers. This is a generalization of the series expansion over spherical harmonics and spherical Bessel functions for spherical geometries.

arxiv-2401-07652.title: Well-posedness and long-term behaviour for a troposphere wave propagation model
arxiv-2401-07652.creator: Paul Holst, Jens D.M. Rademacher
arxiv-2401-07652.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate a model recently derived by A. Constantin and R.S. Johnson for nonlinear wave propagation in the troposphere, particularly the ’morning glory’ cloud pattern. We consider the model with natural Dirichlet boundary conditions for the vertical velocity at the top of the troposphere, and thus introduce a new pressure term.

arxiv-2402-07325.title: Adaptive Voronoi-based Column Selection Methods for Interpretable Dimensionality Reduction
arxiv-2402-07325.creator: Maria Emelianenko, Guy B. Oldaker IV
arxiv-2402-07325.description: Abstract In data analysis, there continues to be a need for interpretable dimensionality reduction methods whereby instrinic meaning associated with the data is retained in the reduced space. Standard approaches such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) fail at this task. A popular alternative is the CUR decomposition.

arxiv-2412-13572.title: A Model-Based Clustering Approach for Bounded Data Using Transformation-Based Gaussian Mixture Models
arxiv-2412-13572.creator: Luca Scrucca
arxiv-2412-13572.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Luca Scrucca. The clustering of bounded data presents unique challenges in statistical analysis due to the constraints imposed on the data values. This paper introduces a novel method for model-based clustering specifically designed for bounded data. Building on the transformation-based approach to Gaussian mixture density estimation introduced by Scrucca, (2019) , we extend this framework to develop a probabilistic clustering algorithm for data with bounded support that allows for accurate clustering while respecting the natural bounds of the variables.

arxiv-2503-19472.title: The metal-poorest tail of the Galactic halo: hypothesis on its origin from precise spectral analysis Thanks: XXX
arxiv-2503-19472.creator: Riano E. Giribaldi, Laura Magrini, Martina Rossi, Anish M. Amarsi, Donatella Romano, Davide Massari
arxiv-2503-19472.description: Abstract Context. The origin of the Galactic halo is one of the fundamental topics linking the study of galaxy formation and evolution to cosmology. Aims. We aim at deriving precise and accurate stellar parameters, Mg abundances, and ages for a sample of metal-poor stars with [Fe/H] < − 2 <-2 dex from high signal-to-noise and high resolution spectra. Methods.

arxiv-2505-13230.title: Implicit bias produces neural scaling laws in learning curves, from perceptrons to deep networks
arxiv-2505-13230.creator: Francesco D’Amico, Dario Bocchi, Matteo Negri
arxiv-2505-13230.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francesco D’Amico, Dario Bocchi, Matteo Negri. Scaling laws in deep learning – empirical power-law relationships linking model performance to resource growth – have emerged as simple yet striking regularities across architectures, datasets, and tasks. These laws are particularly impactful in guiding the design of state-of-the-art models, since they quantify the benefits of increasing data or model size, and hint at the foundations of interpretability in machine learning. However, most studies focus on asymptotic behavior at the end of training.

arxiv-2510-16204.title: Decoherence-free subspaces in the noisy dynamics of discrete-step quantum walks in a photonic lattice
arxiv-2510-16204.creator: Rajesh Asapanna, Clément Hainaut, Alberto Amo, Álvaro Gómez-León
arxiv-2510-16204.description: Abstract We study the noisy dynamics of periodically driven, discrete-step quantum walks in a one-dimensional photonic lattice. We find that in the bulk, temporal noise that is constant within a Floquet period leads to decoherence-free momentum subspaces, whereas fully random noise destroys coherence in a few time-steps.

It may also be prepared by oxidizing the trimethylene glycol obtained by the action of hydrobromic acid on allylbromide.

pmc-11350198.title: Epidemiological characteristics and early predict model of children Mycoplasma Pneumoniae Pneumonia outbreaks after the COVID-19 in Shandong
pmc-11350198.creator: Qian Zeng, Yurong Li, Yuanyuan Yue, Min Wang, Chun Yang, Xin Lv
pmc-11350198.description: Since October 2023, a significant outbreak of Mycoplasma Pneumoniae Pneumonia (MPP) has been observed in children in northern China. Chinese health authorities have attributed this epidemiological to immune debt resulting from the relaxation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) control measures.

pmc-11504867.title: The Functional and Prognostic Impact of TIGIT Expression on Bone Marrow NK Cells in Core Binding Factor-Acute Myeloid Leukemia Patients at Diagnosis
pmc-11504867.creator: Dai-Hong Xie, Jun Wang, Kai Sun, Zong-Yan Shi, Ya-Zhe Wang, Yan Chang, Xiao-Ying Yuan, Yan-Rong Liu, Hao Jiang, Qian Jiang, Xiao-Jun Huang, Ya-Zhen Qin
pmc-11504867.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The effect of the expression of the newly identified immune checkpoint, T cell immunoglobulin and immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibition motif domain (TIGIT) on NK cells in core binding factor-acute myeloid leukemia (CBF-AML) remains to be investigated. Methods: Fresh bone marrow samples from a total of 39 newly diagnosed CBF-AML patients and 25 healthy donors (HDs) were collected for testing the phenotype and function state of total NK, CD56bright, and CD56dim NK cell subsets after in vitro stimulation.

pmc-11642060.title: Unveiling the Future of Cardiac Care: A Review of Gene Therapy in Cardiomyopathies
pmc-11642060.creator: Damiano Venturiello, Pier Giorgio Tiberi, Francesco Perulli, Giulia Nardoianni, Leonardo Guida, Carlo Barsali, Carlo Terrone, Alessandro Cianca, Camilla Lustri, Matteo Sclafani, Giacomo Tini, Emanuele Barbato, Beatrice Musumeci, Anastasios Lymperopoulos
pmc-11642060.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). For years, the treatment of many cardiomyopathies has been solely focused on symptom management. However, cardiomyopathies have a genetic substrate, and directing therapy towards the pathophysiology rather than the epiphenomenon of the disease may be a winning strategy. Gene therapy involves the insertion of genes or the modification of existing ones and their regulatory elements through strategies like gene replacement and gene editing.

pmc-11714356.title: Born during World War II: Associations with lower incident dementia
pmc-11714356.creator: Sotiria Moza, Nikolaos Scarmeas, Mary Yannakoulia, Efthimios Dardiotis, Georgios M Hadjigeorgiou, Paraskevi Sakka, Mary H Kosmidis
pmc-11714356.description: BackgroundPrior longitudinal studies have found that individuals born during World War II and the postwar period had lower incident dementia (Tom et al., 2020) than previous generations, a finding contradictory to research indicating early‐life stressors as adverse events for late‐life cognition. This study aimed to further explore this association and underlying factors.

pmc-12139640.title: The Electrocardiographic Conundrum in a Patient on Methadone Maintenance Therapy and Cannabis Coingestion: A Case Report of a Heartbreaking Puzzle
pmc-12139640.creator: Muhammad Adnan Zaman, Amna Amir, Lou Mastrine
pmc-12139640.description: Methadone is considered relatively safe when compared to other opioids. Methadone, however, can cause respiratory depression and QT prolongation. Among patients on methadone maintenance therapy, the rate of cannabis use is high. Multiple hypotheses, including the ‘exit hypothesis’ or ‘the cannabis association with reduced opioid use,’ need validation and further research.

pmc-12540899.title: Correction: The Activation of G Protein-Coupled Receptor 30 (GPR30) Inhibits Proliferation of Estrogen Receptor Negative Breast Cancer Cells in vitro and in vivo

pmc-12653076.title: Combining Natural and Microbial Insecticides with Diatomaceous Earth for Effective Management of Prostephanus truncatus
pmc-12653076.creator: Demeter Lorentha S Gidari, Maria C Boukouvala, Constantin S Filintas, Anna Skourti, Nickolas G Kavallieratos, Pasquale Trematerra
pmc-12653076.description: Simple SummaryThe larger grain borer, Prostephanus truncatus, is a serious pest of stored maize. In this study, diatomaceous earth (DE) was tested against P. truncatus, alone and in combination with three other natural or microbial insecticidal agents: spinosad, abamectin, and the entomopathogenic fungus (EPF) Beauveria bassiana, at low concentrations, at 25 and 30 °C.

pmc-12831391.title: A certain set of signs that could be compatible with Kabuki syndrome: a case report of an Iranian girl and review of literature
pmc-12831391.creator: Fatemeh Owlia, Maryam Irannezhad, Zahra Bahrololoomi, Shima Mosallaeipour
pmc-12831391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundKabuki syndrome is a rare congenital disorder with multisystem involvement and distinctive craniofacial features. While mutations in KMT2D and KDM6A are commonly associated, approximately 20–25% of patient cases lack molecular confirmation and require phenotype-based diagnosis.Case presentationsWe report a case of a 6-year-old Iranian girl presenting with multiple hallmark features of Kabuki syndrome type II, including characteristic facial morphology, skeletal anomalies, and prominent oral findings. Dental manifestations included hypodontia, malocclusion, delayed eruption, and ectopic molars.

pmc-13063115.title: Hospital variation in the treatment of cT1a renal cancer
pmc-13063115.creator: Cato Caroline Bresser, Paul Bastiaan van der Nat, Hilin Yildirim, Bart Jean Pieter Kersten, Hein Johannes Josephus Leenarts, Katja Karen Helmi Aben, Patricia Jeannelle Zondervan, Lea Magdalena Dijksman, Pepijn Dione Polm, Mirjam Marjolein Garvelink, Harm Hubertus Edmundus van Melick, Wouterus Antoni
pmc-13063115.description: ObjectivesTo evaluate treatment patterns and inter‐hospital variation of cT1a renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in seven Dutch teaching hospitals.Patients and methodsIn this historical multicenter cohort study, adults diagnosed with cT1a renal cancer (2019–2022) were identified through the Netherlands Cancer Registry. Clinical data were extracted from electronic records. Primary outcome was initial treatment. Descriptive statistics and subgroup analyses assessed variation.

pmc-13115892.title: Synergistic Antimicrobial and Antiviral Efficacy of Chitosan–Silver Nanocomposites Against Major Pathogens of Bombyx mori: In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluations
pmc-13115892.creator: Tao Xu, Zi Liang, Xinhao Jiao, Lulai Wang, Haoran Zhong, Ping Wu
pmc-13115892.description: Simple SummaryDiseases caused by viruses and bacteria are a major threat to silkworm (Bombyx mori) health and seriously limit silk production worldwide. Current disease control methods often rely on the extensive use of antimicrobial agents and chemical disinfectants, which contribute to antimicrobial resistance and environmental pollution, respectively.

pmc-13380272.title: Effectiveness of Topical Anesthesia in Patients Undergoing Phacoemulsification Cataract Surgery versus Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Cataract Surgery
pmc-13380272.creator: Meiyi Zhu, Yimei Liu, Zongsheng Zeng, Ziling Zhang, Guangbin Zhang
pmc-13380272.description: PurposeTo assess the effectiveness of topical anesthesia in patients undergoing phacoemulsification cataract surgery (PCS) and femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery (FLACS), and investigate an efficient anesthesia protocol for FLACS.MethodsNon-randomized, prospective cohort study. In this study, patients undergoing cataract surgery self-selected their preferred technique (PCS or FLACS; n = 100 eyes per cohort) and received three topical anesthesia applications prior to phacoemulsification.

pmc-13509163.title: Phage Therapy Is Partially Successful in Rescuing Hornworms from Pseudomonas Infections
pmc-13509163.creator: Jennifer L. Wilcox, Emma K. Spencer, Tracey L. Peters, Craig R. Miller, James J. Bull
pmc-13509163.description: Background: Phage therapy is one of the few alternatives to confront the tide of drug-resistant bacteria. Yet phage therapy is often applied knowing little more than that the therapeutic phages can grow on the infecting bacterium. The lack of convenient, inexpensive infection models slows progress in discovering principles that may improve phage therapy success.

uslaw-usc-t28-s2071.title: 28 U.S.C. § 2071 — Rule-making power generally
uslaw-usc-t28-s2071.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s2071.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part V (Procedure); Chapter 131 (Rules Of Courts). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The Supreme Court and all courts established by Act of Congress may from time to time prescribe rules for the conduct of their business. Such rules shall be consistent with Acts of Congress and rules of practice and procedure.
